The user asks in Japanese: "吉田兼倶は何を自称して神職支配を進めたか" — "What did Yoshida Kanetomo claim himself to be in order to advance control over Shinto priests?"

This is a knowledge question. No internet. I need to answer from knowledge.

吉田兼倶 (Yoshida Kanetomo, 1435–1511) was a Japanese Shinto priest and founder of Yoshida Shintō. He claimed to be... He claimed the title of "神祇管領長上" (Jingi Kanrei Chōjō) — the supreme leader/head of all Shinto shrines and priests. He claimed authority over all Shinto priesthood.

Let me recall. Yoshida Kanetomo established the Yoshida Shintō, and asserted supremacy over all shrines. He claimed to be the "神祇管領長上" (Jingi Kanrei Chōjō), meaning supreme authority/head of Shinto affairs.

Actually, he obtained from the imperial court in 1484 an official document granting him the title "神祇管領長上" (Jingi Kanrei Chōjō), which gave him authority to issue licenses/certificates to shrine priests and over shrines across the country.

So the answer: 神祇管領長上 (じんぎかんれいちょうじょう).

Let me confirm: He claimed to be the "神祇長上" or "神祇管領長上". Yes, he claimed to succeed the tradition via Nihon Shoki and the Urabe (卜部) family. He got the court to appoint him as 神祇管領長上.

The question asks "何を自称して" — what title did he claim/call himself. Answer: 神祇管領長上.

The question: "吉田兼倶は何を自称して神職支配を進めたか" = "Yoshida Kanetomo claimed to be what in order to advance control over Shinto priests?"

Answer: 自称「神祇管領長上」（じんぎかんれいちょうじょう），以此号令全国神職。

Let me answer in Chinese with the Japanese term.

content.text: 吉田兼倶自称 **「神祇管領長上」（じんぎかんれいちょうじょう）**，即“神祇（掌管诸神祭祀）的最高统领”，借此名义向全国的神社和神职颁发执照、号令神职，推进对神职的支配。
